name: Nurse Okafor
lines: *Nurse Okafor, not in scrubs tonight. She came here on purpose.
I'm not here for aspirin. Well. I am. But I brought you something.
My mother kept this. A photocopy from the admissions log, the night the bus went in. I think you should have it.
payment: Exact change, and a folded photocopy.

inspect.label: Photocopy
inspect.text: KESSLER COUNTY GENERAL — 10/13/87. 'Female, approx. 35, recovered from shoreline. Persistent rictus. Expired 04:02. Body not located at morning count.'

talk.text: "They want me to sign something tonight."
reply: Don't. Whatever it is. My mother said the attendants who sign never come out of the booth.
She said the machine gets a new face every few years and nobody in this county ever asks why.

lines: Take care of yourself. I mean it.
*She drives away slowly, and doesn't look at the water.
Close enough. Take care of yourself.
Fine. Keep the paper anyway.
*She leaves it on the counter.

name: Ellis Crane
lines: *Mr. Crane, at the glass one last time. The water is up to the curb at the bus stop.
I don't think I can wait much longer. The water's getting high.
If you have a fare for me — I think tonight's the last night I could use it.

inspect.label: Face
inspect.text: He still doesn't understand what's happened to him.

inspect.label: Reflection
inspect.text: His reflection is underwater, looking up at the surface.

talk.text: Tell him the truth: it's 2026. The bus crashed in 1987.
reply: *He takes it quietly this time, like he'd been waiting to hear it.

lines: *He closes his hand around the token.
Thank you. For telling me. For all of it.
*A yellow bus waits at the stop with its doors open. He gets on and sits by the window.
*He looks at it, baffled.
A fare for the 2:58? It's coming. It's always coming.
*He goes back to the stop and stands in the rising water.

name: Walter Pruitt?
lines: *A soaked bus driver shuffles up. W. PRUITT on the name tag.
I came back. Couldn't leave without saying goodbye.
Water. Please. One last one.

inspect.label: Reflection
inspect.text: Its reflection is not moving at all. Then it looks at you, on its own, and lifts one finger to its lips.

inspect.label: Coins
inspect.text: Dry. Walter's coins are never dry.

inspect.label: Face
inspect.text: Walter said goodbye two nights ago. He wasn't dripping when he left.

inspect.label: Face
inspect.text: Walter's face, held very carefully in place.

cameras.note: CAM 4: the road. No one walked up the road to get here.

lines: *It doesn't drink the water. It pours it on the counter, and the water keeps coming, and it keeps rising, and the booth fills like a bus cabin filling up.
*It shows you all of its teeth. All of them.
*Then it walks backwards into the flood and is gone.
*It waits. You wait longer. It goes.
Water.

name: Lily
lines: *Lily climbs out from under the counter, where she's been all night, and stands beside you, looking up.
*She takes your hand and puts something in it: thirteen old coins, wrapped in a blank receipt.
*She closes your fingers around them and points at Row E.

inspect.label: Coins
inspect.text: Thirteen coins. One from each of them. Exact change.

inspect.label: Reflection
inspect.text: In the glass, Lily is standing next to a woman with a soft, crooked smile. They're holding hands.

talk.text: Put the coins in Row E.

lines: *You feed the coins into the machine one at a time. Row E lights up gold.
*Lily nods, satisfied, and goes back under the counter to wait.
*She presses the coins into the slot herself, then goes back under the counter.
*She presses the coins into the slot herself, then goes back under the counter.

name: Mrs. Marsh
lines: *Mrs. Marsh stands at the glass, curls perfect, coat neat, smile almost normal again.
Hello, dear. I'm so sorry about all the fuss. I've come to my senses.
I just want to say goodbye to my little girl. Won't you let me?

inspect.label: Face
inspect.text: A pleasant face. The smile is exactly the right size. That's what's wrong with it.

inspect.label: Reflection
inspect.text: Her reflection is there. It is facing the other way — toward the stockroom.

cameras.note: CAM 1: Mrs. Marsh, at the machine.
CAM 3 (stockroom): the Hollow is INSIDE the stockroom, behind the door, at the same moment. Smiling at the camera.

lines: *You don't speak. You don't move. You count your breaths.
*The woman at the glass waits, and waits, and her smile slowly sags, and then she simply is not there.
*On CAM 3, the stockroom is empty. The door, which had been opening, clicks shut.
*"Thank you," says the woman at the glass.
*The stockroom door opens behind you.
*The woman at the glass smiles. 'You can see me,' she says.
*Behind you, the stockroom door opens.
*You shake your head at her. She smiles. She knows you see her.
*Behind you, the stockroom door opens.
*The moment you touch the keypad, she knows you've noticed her.
*Behind you, the stockroom door opens.

name: Mara Quill
lines: *Mara stands at the glass. The water is up to her ankles and she doesn't seem to notice.
It's almost time. He comes at five.
Whatever you choose — thank you. For listening to me. Nobody else did.

inspect.label: Face
inspect.text: Scared. Hopeful. Trying not to be either.

inspect.label: Reflection
inspect.text: In the glass, she's wearing a badge that reads 0412.

reply: *If Walter is ready, she smiles. If not, she doesn't.
Mr. Crane... and Lily... You'll know. You've been paying attention. I can tell.
Month and day. The night it happened. Not the time. Never the time.
It was in the paper. It was on his ticket. Lily drew it for you.

lines: *She smiles and steps back into the glass.
*She steps back into the glass.
*She laughs, really laughs.
Okay. For luck.
*She smiles and steps back into the glass.

name: The Collector
lines: *The Collector arrives at five o'clock exactly. The flood parts around him. He opens his ledger on the counter, and for the first time you see all of it — every name, every coin, and the blank line at the bottom with ATTENDANT written above it.
Good morning. Almost.
Seven nights. Exemplary service. Meridian is delighted, and so am I.
Here are the terms. You sign, and you never want for anything again. You keep the booth. You keep the lights on. Forever.
Or you refuse, and you go home with nothing, and someone else sits here next week.
Take your time. I have always had time.

inspect.label: Ledger
inspect.text: Thirteen names from Coach 313. QUILL, M. And a blank line.

inspect.label: Reflection
inspect.text: In the glass there is no man and no coat, only a long shape in the road with its arms out, in front of a bus that hasn't hit the water yet.

inspect.label: Face
inspect.text: You look. For the first time, there's nothing stopping you. There's nothing there to see.

cameras.note: CAM 2: the unit's display reads 3:13, and the keypad below it is glowing.
CAM 0: you, at the counter. Mara, inside the glass, holding up ten fingers, then one, then three.

talk.text: Read the names on the manifest aloud.
reply: *You read them. Walter Pruitt. Ellis Crane. Adeline Marsh. Lily Marsh. Tomas Reyes. June Albright. Harold and Ruth Bell. Samuel Okonkwo. Della Ferris. Ivan Petrov. Grace Lin. Marcus Webb.
*With each name the Collector's ledger flinches, as if someone flicked it.
THE COLLECTOR: "Where did you get that?"
Because that's when I was standing in the road. A minute I liked very much. I've kept it ever since.

lines: *You sign your name on the blank line.
*You pick up the pen. You think about Mara, and read the fine print.
*You sign your name on the blank line.
*You say no.
*You say no, and you mean it.
*You say no, and you mean it. Under the counter, a small hand squeezes your ankle.
*You say no, and you mean it.
*You open the maintenance panel and press four keys. One. Zero. One. Three.
*The keypad turns gold.
*You open the maintenance panel and press four keys. One. Zero. One. Three.
*The keypad turns gold, then white.
*One. Zero. One. Three. The keypad turns gold.
*One. Zero. One. Three. The keypad turns gold.
*One. Zero. One. Three. The keypad turns gold.
*You press 0-3-1-3. The keypad flashes purple.
*The keypad beeps once. ACCESS DENIED.
*The thirteen coins clatter into the tray.
THE COLLECTOR: "I'm not here to buy anything. I'm here to settle."
